title: San Diego automated rent price-fixing prohibition
requirement: No person may sell, license or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and no landlord may use one to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in San Diego.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego; applies to sellers and licensors of algorithmic devices and to landlords.

applicability.other: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego

exemptions: Software publishing reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from public information without recommending future rates, and software setting rates under affordable housing program guidelines.
penalty: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; a prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees; each month and each property is a separate violation.
quoted_span:
(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
conflict_note: Effective date is the thirtieth day after final passage, but the date of final passage is blank in this packet.

title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance in affordable housing
requirement: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance limits consideration of arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
coverage_conditions: Residents with arrest or conviction history facing affordable housing decisions in San Francisco.
quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.

title: San Francisco just cause eviction requirement
requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of the 17 just causes, which must be the dominant motive; lease expiration or a change of ownership is not just cause.
coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, including some tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limitations.

applicability.other: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance

penalty: A landlord who evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
interaction: Just cause eviction provisions apply even to tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limitations.

title: Rent Ordinance rent increase exemptions for new and regulated tenancies
requirement: Tenancies in newly constructed units that first obtained a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, and tenancies with rent regulated by another government agency are exempt from the rent increase limitations.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental units subject to the rent increase limitations of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.

applicability.other: Also Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies and tenancies with rent regulated by another government agency

exemptions: Newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act; some tenancies with rent regulated by another government agency.
citation: S.F. Rent Ordinance, rent increase limitation exemptions
quoted_span: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance. This includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies that are eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency.
interaction: These tenancies are exempt from the Ordinance's rent limits but remain subject to its just cause eviction provisions.

title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase 2026-2027
requirement: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%, found by multiplying the tenant's base rent by .016.
coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units in San Francisco covered by the Rent Ordinance.
citation: S.F. Rent Board, annual allowable rent increase 3/1/26-2/28/27
quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic devices for setting rents
requirement: The sale or use of algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or occupancy levels for San Francisco residential units is prohibited.
coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco; applies to sellers of algorithmic devices and to landlords who use them.
penalty: A tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action against an entity believed to be in violation of the law.
quoted_span: Legislation adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

title: San Francisco relocation payments for no-fault evictions
requirement: A landlord evicting for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation assistance per tenant, capped per unit, plus an added amount for elderly, disabled or minor-child households.
key_value: $8,245.00 per tenant, max $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00
coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation.

applicability.other: Additional amount for each elderly, disabled tenant or household with minor children

exemptions: Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9, not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.

coverage_conditions: Tenant households temporarily displaced for less than 20 days under California Civil Code Section 1947.9.

applicability.other: Temporary displacement for less than 20 days
